page.layout: One page of running text, with a running head and page number at the top. Two headings set in italic, centred, between the paragraphs. No margin notes. Catchword and signature at the foot, lower left and right.

main_text.p: Quia uero difficilis hic locus est, & ad iustificationis negocium, ac ad exhortationem ad patientiam, adhiberi solet, primum sensum eius grammaticū exponemus: deinde propheticū sensum, ex Apostoli Pauli sententia, fideliter declarare stu debimus.
main_text.head: Quid facturos censes Nebucadnezarem & Chaldaeos eius clientes?
main_text.p: Extollent sese ipsos maiorem in modum. nec id cuiquam mirum uideri debet, cum eorum animae nō sint rectae: sed incredulitate distortae, & à Deo auersae. Inflat enim incredulitas, cum sibi uidetur praesidijs satis instructa, & cum successus carni & sanguini gratos illa consequitur: ut exempla summorum in hoc mundo hominum testantur, Alexandri Magni, Pompeij, Marij, Sullae, & multorum aliorum: de quibus dicit Psaltes: Impius in altitudine naris suae non inquirit: omnes cogitationes eius sunt, quod non sit Deus: Psal.io.4.

head.i: Quid aut fideles, interim dum illi emergunt & triumphant, facturos censes?

main_text.p: Fide sua uicturi sunt, patienter ferentes aduersos casus, & certò persuasum ha

page.notes: Heading lines are set in italic type in the original; the first heading is black-letter-free roman italic as shown. Doubtful readings: "stu" at the end of the first paragraph (the printed form is unclear and may be a word fragment such as "istud"; written as "stu" with the rest unclear). "facturos" in the first heading is printed with a long-s-like form; it is read as f with crossbar. The catchword "ben-" and the signature "n" at the foot are read from a small, faint print and may be misread. The word "aut" in the second heading is printed with a superscript bar, read as "aut". Stray marks in the right margin are not text and are left out.
